source.slab2: USGS Slab2 (Hayes et al. 2018, Science 362:58), doi 10.5066/F7PV6JNV; ScienceBase parent item 5aa1b00ee4b0b1c392e86467. Regions: kur = Kamchatka-Kuril Islands-Japan (item 5aa4060de4b0b1c392eaaee2); izu = Izu-Bonin (item 5aa3185ee4b0b1c392ea3f0d); ryu = Ryukyu (item 5aa40aafe4b0b1c392eaaefa). Depth and uncertainty grids thinned from 0.05 to the 0.1 degree lattice and cropped to the catalog box; depth in 0.1 km.
source.volcanoes: Smithsonian Institution Global Volcanism Program, Holocene volcanoes, WFS GVP-VOTW:Smithsonian_VOTW_Holocene_Volcanoes, bbox 122,24,150,46

supp.note: izu_slab2_sup: points of the overturned Izu-Bonin slab; one mean point per 0.2 degree by 25 km cell; [lat, lon, depth_km, ...]

published.note: Values quoted in the essay that cannot be computed from the grids. Carried over from the q-02 audit (temp/japan-audit/q02/pb.out for the rates, EarthByte for the ages); this script does not recompute them.

pacificAgeMa.source: EarthByte 2020 seafloor age grid (age.2020.1.GTS2012.6m.nc), sampled seaward of each trench

rateMmYr.source: PB2002 Euler poles (Bird 2003, PB2002_poles.dat.txt), trench-normal rate PA\OK at the Japan Trench; reproduces PB2002_steps.dat.txt speeds to 0.05 mm/yr

nankaiAgeMa.source: EarthByte 2020 age grid seaward of the Nankai Trough

tohoku.source: Fujiwara et al. 2011 (seafloor displacement); published slip models, Part 6

herp2025.source: HERP Earthquake Research Committee, 2025-09 Nankai Trough summary (jishin.go.jp/main/chousa/25sep_nankai/nankai_gaiyou2_3.pdf, p.3 and p.9): both values given side by side, neither preferred
